hq.admin_console_anatomy:
The admin console lives entirely within this repo at /admin/ — there is no separate repo. It is a Python stdlib http.server SPA (no web framework): admin/server.py routes to ~20 module files (health.py, experiments.py, vector_override.py, etc.), serving admin/static/{index.html, app.js, styles.css}.

TAB ARCHITECTURE (the Experiments tab precedent):
Each tab is a key in the TABS array at admin/static/app.js:53-57. Current 12 tabs: Overview, Experiments, BTC Override, Analytics, Users, System, Health, Features, AI Brief, Build & Deploy, AI Cost, Content. Each tab has a RENDER.<id> async function. Adding a new tab = (1) append [id, label] to TABS, (2) add RENDER.<id> = async () => { ... } that calls a new /api/<id> endpoint, (3) add the GET route in server.py do_GET(), (4) add a panel module admin/<id>.py that reads the relevant data artifacts.

Experiments tab data flow precedent (admin/experiments.py:19): reads site/marketdata/experiments.json (produced by engine/experiments_registry.py nightly), computes live days_until + ready flags, returns JSON to /api/experiments. The VPS clone pulls main within minutes of a push, so the panel always serves committed artifact state — no direct engine calls, no subprocess.

Styling/framework: vanilla JS, no external deps. CSS uses CSS variables (--ok, --warn, --bad, --text, --panel, --muted, --accent, --line). Layout primitives: .grid (auto-fit minmax cards), .card, .section, .kv (key-value rows), .statpill (colored status badges), .meter (progress bars), table/thead/tbody. Dark theme with data-theme="dark" on html. All cards built via the card(title, bodyHtml) helper function.

Auth + config flow: when ADMIN_DEPLOYED=1, password-gated via signed session cookie + double-submit CSRF. Config edits (flag toggles) in deployed mode go through the GitHub Contents API (admin/github_config.py), not local file writes. The VPS reads committed artifacts — a new tab's panel.py reads from the local /opt/macro clone which mirrors main.
hq.auth_and_deploy:
DEPLOYMENT PIPELINE: VPS at 146.190.142.17. Caddy reverse-proxies admin.mastermind-x.com → 127.0.0.1:8787. Systemd unit: /etc/systemd/system/admin.service (admin/deploy/admin.service) runs `python -m admin --deployed --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787`. Env secrets in /etc/macro-admin.env (root-only 0600): ADMIN_DEPLOYED=1, ADMIN_PASSWORD, ADMIN_SESSION_SECRET, SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, optionally GH_TOKEN.

AUTH MODEL: session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict) + CSRF double-submit (admin_csrf cookie readable by JS). Every /api/* route except /healthz, /api/session, login/logout requires a valid session when ADMIN_DEPLOYED=1. Loopback host check prevents DNS-rebinding.

EXACT PIPELINE FOR ADDING A NEW TAB:
1. Add panel module admin/neural_web.py (reads data/neuralweb/*.json + data/reflexes/*/firings.jsonl + data/neuralweb/governance.jsonl). The VPS clone at /opt/macro has these as git-tracked files.
2. Add import in admin/server.py line 30 (the single import block).
3. Add GET route: `if path == "/api/neural_web": return self._json(neural_web.panel())` inside do_GET() after auth check.
4. Add RENDER.neural_web = async () => { ... } in admin/static/app.js.
5. Append ["neural_web", "Neural Web"] (or split into multiple tabs) to the TABS array at app.js:53-57.
6. Push to main → Caddy serves static files from /opt/macro/admin/static/ (no separate build step — static files are served directly by the Python http.server from the repo clone). The VPS systemd service auto-restarts on code change via `git pull` in the deploy script, or manual `systemctl restart admin.service`.

Note: the VPS clone is effectively read-only for the panel itself — data artifacts land there via the GitHub Actions daily.yml pipeline (daily engine run commits to main, VPS pulls). The panel reads committed artifact state only, never runs engine code.

push.w6b_design_rec:
VERDICT: Sub-hour on existing lanes suffices for v1. A VPS endpoint is NOT justified now.

EVIDENCE BASE:

1. No reflex currently meets the minutes-class acceptance criterion in production. The w4w6_scout.json registry_design_rec states explicitly: "W6b push tier (VPS FastAPI webhook / systemd timer) is reserved for reflexes where end-to-end latency <= 5 min is the acceptance criterion, measured in production." Of the five candidate reflexes enumerated in the registry schema (whitehouse_alert, regime_self_heal, btc_flash_crash, commodity_shock, circuit_breaker_trip), only circuit_breaker_trip carries push_tier: true — and its trigger is embedded inside the nightly collect run (daily.yml 02:00 UTC), not an intraday event. None of the three priority-migration reflexes (whitehouse_alert, btc_flash_crash, regime_self_heal) carry push_tier: true in the registry design.

2. Existing lanes deliver 30-75 min latency. The two 30-min sentinel lanes (vector-sentinel, commodity-sentinel) and the intraday fastpath are all in the 30-75 min effective range. The whitehouse sentinel is 60-105 min. For alert-triage push (the W6 unification step), the path is: event fires a sentinel → event appended to JSONL → push_priority_alerts() is called from the SAME sentinel run and dispatches Telegram before the commit step. That collapses push latency to the sentinel's own execution time (~seconds), not the next cron tick. So the existing sentinel architecture already achieves sub-minute push latency from trigger to Telegram dispatch IF push_priority_alerts() is called inline inside the sentinel script (not deferred to the next fastpath tick). No VPS endpoint is needed for this.

3. Which 2-3 reflexes would earn a VPS endpoint (if latency evidence changes):
   - btc_flash_crash: 24/7 coverage is the key argument. If the 30-min Coinbase candle poll is too coarse for a genuine flash-crash detection use case (e.g. a 10-min crash recovers before the sentinel fires), a VPS systemd timer running every 5 min with a websocket or REST REST call would justify the endpoint. NOT justified today — no measured miss has been documented.
   - circuit_breaker_trip: a data-source dead state during RTH that is not surfaced for 30-75 min is a real operational cost. This is the strongest candidate for a VPS endpoint because it is purely operational (not a signal) and the latency cost is concrete. Push_tier: true already in the registry design.
   - whitehouse_alert: Opus evaluation latency (~10-20s) is already the bottleneck, not the sentinel cron. A VPS endpoint would not help unless the RSS poll itself is the bottleneck (it is not — it is fast).

4. The operator Article-2 decision for enabling push_priority_alerts():
   Enabling push_priority_alerts() in engine/alert_triage.py is an Article-2 operator event. The constitution defines Article 2 as: any action that raises a ranking, ordering, or alert priority in a user-visible channel. push_priority_alerts() dispatching a Telegram card is exactly that — it surfaces a priority score to the user's phone. The operator must decide: (a) confirm the priority floor (default 60 = act-tier + critical severity + any recency − 10 buffer), (b) confirm explicit suppress flags for rotation entered_book/left_book/leadership_rotation and altdata convergence without validated IC, (c) confirm the 6-hour window_hours dedup window, and (d) confirm the push_sent.jsonl append-only single-writer path does not conflict with any in-flight workflow (it is a new file, so no race). The operator decision is a single config commit to engine/alert_triage.py (or a new config/push_alerts.yml) — not a VPS change.

5. Measured-latency acceptance design (the gate before a VPS endpoint is justified):
   Before building a VPS endpoint, run push_priority_alerts() inline in the three sentinel scripts for 2-4 weeks and log (trigger_ts, push_ts, delta_seconds) to data/alert_triage/push_latency.jsonl. If any reflex class shows: (a) delta > 10 min in more than 5% of firings AND (b) a documented case where the delay caused a missed actionable window, the VPS endpoint earns its build. Without that log, the endpoint is speculative infrastructure. The existing mastermind.service FastAPI (:8001) is already live and could host the webhook endpoint with a one-file code change + rsync + restart — the build cost is low, but the operational cost (another failure surface, another service to monitor) is not zero, and the latency benefit is unproven until the log exists.
